sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In the beginning, there was design.
sentences.zh: 最初，有了设计。

sentences.en: At least, according to designer and author Will Lidwell,
sentences.zh: 至少，根据设计师兼作家威尔·利德韦尔的说法，

sentences.en: design is the oldest human discipline, older than humanity itself.
sentences.zh: 设计是最古老的人类学科，比人类本身还要古老。

sentences.en: And Will believes that in this oldest of old disciplines, everything ever designed
sentences.zh: 威尔坚信，在这个最古老的学科中，所有曾经被设计出来的东西——

sentences.en: spaceships, buildings, pyramids, weapons, clothing, artwork, everything
sentences.zh: 飞船、建筑、金字塔、武器、服装、艺术品，万事万物——

sentences.en: can be traced back to a single designed object, the first designed object.
sentences.zh: 都可以追溯到一个单一的设计物品，即第一个被设计的物品。

sentences.en: This is as close to a Genesis object as we have.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是我们所拥有的最接近创世之物的存在了。

sentences.en: I mean, this is where it all began.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是一切的起点。

sentences.en: This is where it all began.
sentences.zh: 这就是一切的起点。

sentences.en: If design had its own Cosmos series, this would be episode one.
sentences.zh: 如果设计有它自己的《宇宙》系列纪录片，这就是第一集。

sentences.en: I think this is the greatest, grandest, like most interesting story in the field of design.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是设计领域中最伟大、最宏大、最有趣的故事。

sentences.en: It has it all.
sentences.zh: 它应有尽有。

sentences.en: Mystery, entry, controversy.
sentences.zh: 悬疑、入门、争议。

sentences.en: We are on the edge of our seats, Will.
sentences.zh: 我们都听得悬心吊胆，威尔。

sentences.en: Wait for it.
sentences.zh: 拭目以待吧。

sentences.en: I need like the drum roll here.
sentences.zh: 我这里需要来点戏剧性的鼓点。

sentences.en: The first designed object was the Acheulean hand axe.
sentences.zh: 第一个被设计的物品是阿舍利手斧。

sentences.en: The Acheulean hand axe, ladies and gentlemen.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，阿舍利手斧。

sentences.en: Actually, it doesn't look like an axe at all.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它看起来一点也不像斧头。

sentences.en: There's no handle.
sentences.zh: 没有手柄。

sentences.en: There's no metal.
sentences.zh: 没有金属。

sentences.en: Honestly, it should be called the Acheulean pointy hand rock.
sentences.zh: 说实话，它应该被称为阿舍利尖锐手头石。

sentences.en: A hand axe is made of rock, and it's teardrop shaped.
sentences.zh: 手斧是用石头制成的，呈泪滴状。

sentences.en: And if you join your hands together, as if to pray, fingers together and thumbs in,
sentences.zh: 如果你把双手合十，就像做祈祷那样，手指并拢，大拇指内收，

sentences.en: this is almost the exact shape and size of an Acheulean hand axe.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就是阿舍利手斧确切的形状和大小。

sentences.en: The term Acheulean refers to where the first specimens were found,
sentences.zh: 阿舍利这个术语指的是发现第一批标本的地方，

sentences.en: which was a dig site in St. Acheule, France.
sentences.zh: 也就是法国圣阿舍尔的一个发掘遗址。

sentences.en: But they've been found in a lot of other places.
sentences.zh: 但它们在许多其他地方也被发现过。

sentences.en: We find that Acheulean tools are found almost exclusively in Africa, in Europe, and South Asia.
sentences.zh: 我们发现阿舍利工具几乎只在非洲、欧洲和南亚出土。

sentences.en: This is Terence Deacon.
sentences.zh: 这位是特伦斯·迪肯。

sentences.en: I'm Terence Deacon.
sentences.zh: 我是特伦斯·迪肯。

sentences.en: I'm a professor of biological anthropology at the University of California, Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 我是加利福尼亚大学伯克利分校的生物人类学教授。

sentences.en: And Berkeley has a whole bunch of samples of these hand axes.
sentences.zh: 伯克利收藏了大量这种手斧的样本。

sentences.en: There's another hand axe.
sentences.zh: 这里还有另一把手斧。

sentences.en: You can see that it's not quite so symmetric and nice, although it's sharp at this edge.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到它没有那么对称和完美，尽管它的这个边缘很锋利。

sentences.en: Some are sharp all along the entire perimeter.
sentences.zh: 有些手斧整个周长都很锋利。

sentences.en: Some aren't.
sentences.zh: 有些则不然。

sentences.en: Some are perfectly symmetrical, and some are not.
sentences.zh: 有些完全对称，有些则不对称。

sentences.en: But those hand axes in the UC Berkeley basement aren't actual primordial hand axes.
sentences.zh: 但加州大学伯克利分校地下室里的那些手斧并不是真正的原始手斧。

sentences.en: These are replicas made by graduate students.
sentences.zh: 这些是研究生制作的复制品。

sentences.en: Yes, graduate students.
sentences.zh: 没错，研究生。

sentences.en: In fact, there have been courses here in which one of the challenges is to make tools.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这里曾开设过相关的课程，其中的挑战之一就是制作工具。

sentences.en: And the point of this challenge for the graduate students
sentences.zh: 研究生们进行这项挑战的意义在于，

sentences.en: is to see how involved this process is in making one of these pointy rocks,
sentences.zh: 去了解制作这些尖石头到底有多复杂，

sentences.en: the way the early humans would have.
sentences.zh: 就像早期人类所做的那样。

sentences.en: You break off big pieces with large rocks and large strikes,
sentences.zh: 你用大石头猛烈敲击，敲下大块碎片，

sentences.en: and then you break off these little edges.
sentences.zh: 然后你再敲下这些小边缘。

sentences.en: You shape the edge with smaller pieces.
sentences.zh: 用较小的碎片来修整边缘。

sentences.en: I just love the image of a bunch of grad students sitting around smashing rocks together.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢一群研究生坐在一起砸石头的画面了。

sentences.en: And sometimes they have to do it for a while.
sentences.zh: 有时他们得这么干上一阵子。

sentences.en: Someone really practiced at it can make a hand axe in something like 15 minutes to a half hour.
sentences.zh: 一个熟练的人制作一把手斧大概需要 15 分钟到半小时。

sentences.en: But to make a really fine tool, a really carefully shaped tool,
sentences.zh: 但要制作一把真正精致的工具，一把精心塑造的工具，

sentences.en: you're probably talking about an hour to two hours.
sentences.zh: 你可能需要花上一到两个小时。

sentences.en: Acheulean hand axes require time, effort, and skill to make.
sentences.zh: 制作阿舍利手斧需要时间、精力和技巧。

sentences.en: They were a product of a design process.
sentences.zh: 它们是设计过程的产物。

sentences.en: The first design process.
sentences.zh: 最初的设计过程。

sentences.en: But the Acheulean hand axe was not the first tool.
sentences.zh: 但阿舍利手斧并不是最早的工具。

sentences.en: The first tool was...
sentences.zh: 最早的工具是……

sentences.en: Basically a rock that is chipped with just a handful of major strikes to produce a few sharp edges.
sentences.zh: 基本上只经过几下重击来产生几个锋利边缘的碎裂岩石。

sentences.en: Not very sophisticated tools.
sentences.zh: 并不是非常复杂的工具。

sentences.en: Anthropologists call these old wand tools.
sentences.zh: 人类学家称这些为旧石器工具。

sentences.en: Our Homo habilis ancestors used them to bash open bones and scrape meat off of them
sentences.zh: 大约两百万年前，我们的能人祖先用它们来砸开骨头并刮下上面的肉。

sentences.en: around two million years ago.
sentences.zh: 大约两百万年前。

sentences.en: Though this kind of technique isn't unique to humans.
sentences.zh: 不过这种技术并非人类所独有。

sentences.en: This can be done even by South American monkeys, the capuchin monkeys.
sentences.zh: 南美洲的猴子，也就是卷尾猴，也能做到这一点。

sentences.en: They get these large pine nuts and they have hammer stones that they can then lift up
sentences.zh: 它们找到这些大松子，手里拿着锤石，

sentences.en: and bash these things until they open them.
sentences.zh: 高高举起并砸开这些坚果直到它们裂开。

sentences.en: They know what they want to achieve.
sentences.zh: 它们知道自己想达到什么目的。

sentences.en: But they actually simply go out and select something that will accomplish that.
sentences.zh: 但它们实际上只是出去挑选能实现这一目标的东西。

sentences.en: Rather than actually design something.
sentences.zh: 而不是真正去设计什么东西。

sentences.en: Chimpanzees in, for example, stripping the leaves and the side branches off a little branch,
sentences.zh: 例如，黑猩猩剥去小树枝上的树叶和侧枝，

sentences.en: they can stick it down a termite nest and get the termites to bite it.
sentences.zh: 然后把树枝伸进白蚁巢穴里引诱白蚁咬住它。

sentences.en: And so they can eat the termites that way.
sentences.zh: 这样它们就可以吃白蚁了。

sentences.en: So this requires cunning, yes.
sentences.zh: 所以这需要狡黠，没错。

sentences.en: But craft, not really.
sentences.zh: 但要说手艺，其实谈不上。

sentences.en: So early humans understood the importance of old wand tools, those sharp rocks.
sentences.zh: 所以早期人类理解旧石器工具（那些锋利的石头）的重要性。

sentences.en: And they realized that they could fashion more precise tools by sharpening rocks purposefully.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到通过有目的地打磨石头，他们可以打造出更精准的工具。

sentences.en: So it's not just adventitious production.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是偶然的产物。

sentences.en: Now it's planned production.
sentences.zh: 现在这是有计划的生产。

sentences.en: So the hand axe is the first designed object, at least that we can find.
sentences.zh: 因此，手斧是第一个被设计的物品，至少是我们能找到的第一个。

sentences.en: If there were any, say, wooden tools that our human-like ancestors made, those have long
sentences.zh: 如果我们的类人祖先制作过任何木质工具之类的东西，那些东西早就

sentences.en: since disintegrated.
sentences.zh: 已经腐烂分解了。

sentences.en: But even if there are other examples, hand axes are really significant.
sentences.zh: 但即使还有其他例子，手斧也具有非常重大的意义。

sentences.en: With the Acheulean hand axe, with the Acheulean technology showing up, we suddenly now find
sentences.zh: 随着阿舍利手斧和阿舍利技术的出现，我们突然发现

sentences.en: people making people, and I say they're our ancestors, making tools with an end in mind.
sentences.zh: 人类在制造工具——我称他们为我们的祖先——制造工具时带着明确的目的。

sentences.en: They're making them in advance.
sentences.zh: 他们是提前把它们制作出来的。

sentences.en: They almost certainly have to carry them with them.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎肯定得随身携带它们。

sentences.en: They don't just make them on the spot.
sentences.zh: 他们不只是当场制作。

sentences.en: They take time to make them.
sentences.zh: 制作它们需要时间。

sentences.en: They take thought to make them.
sentences.zh: 制作它们需要思考。

sentences.en: And you're shaping them towards a particular shape for some particular use, which we today
sentences.zh: 你把它们塑造成特定的形状是为了某种特定的用途，而这种用途我们今天

sentences.en: don't know.
sentences.zh: 还不得而知。

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不得而知。

sentences.en: We don't know how they were used.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道它们是如何使用的。

sentences.en: That's the crazy mystery here.
sentences.zh: 这就是令人疯狂的谜团所在。

sentences.en: So this is where we get into the intrigue.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始进入引人入胜的部分了。

sentences.en: That's Will Lidwell again.
sentences.zh: 那是威尔·利德韦尔又说话了。

sentences.en: They're ideas, right?
sentences.zh: 这些都是想法，对吧？

sentences.en: So smart people are working on the problem.
sentences.zh: 所以聪明的人们正在研究这个问题。

sentences.en: And there are like three theories.
sentences.zh: 大约有三种理论。

sentences.en: There are more than three.
sentences.zh: 不止三种。

sentences.en: If you want me to talk about more theories, I can talk about more theories.
sentences.zh: 如果你想让我讲更多理论，我可以讲更多理论。

sentences.en: But I'll stop at three unless you tell me otherwise.
sentences.zh: 但除非你另有吩咐，否则我就讲到三种为止。

sentences.en: Will Lidwell has three favorite theories as to why the hand axe appeared.
sentences.zh: 关于手斧为什么会出现，威尔·利德韦尔最喜欢三种理论。

sentences.en: So, all right.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行。

sentences.en: Theory number one, right, of how it's used is the multi-tool theory.
sentences.zh: 关于它是如何被使用的第一个理论是多功能工具理论。

sentences.en: So theory number one is that the Acheulean hand axe was the original Swiss army knife,
sentences.zh: 所以第一种理论是，阿舍利手斧是最初的瑞士军刀，

sentences.en: primarily used for butchering meat.
sentences.zh: 主要用于切割肉类。

sentences.en: But it's also good for breaking open nuts and digging up grubs or whatever else you might
sentences.zh: 但它也很适合砸开坚果、挖出幼虫或者你可能需要的

sentences.en: need.
sentences.zh: 任何其他东西。

sentences.en: And so the strength of this theory is that it fits with wear patterns that you see on a
sentences.zh: 所以这个理论的有力之处在于，它符合在许多被发现的手斧上

sentences.en: lot of the hand axes that are found.
sentences.zh: 看到的磨损痕迹。

sentences.en: Here's the problem with theory number one.
sentences.zh: 这就是第一种理论的问题所在。

sentences.en: In some cases, the full perimeter of the axe is sharp.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，斧头的整个周长都是锋利的。

sentences.en: And remember, this is a hand axe that you're holding in the palm of your hand.
sentences.zh: 记住，这是一把握在你手掌里的手斧。

sentences.en: So if you wanted to use it, there'd be this sharp blade digging into your palm.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想使用它，就会有锋利的刀刃刺入你的手掌。

sentences.en: Another problem with theory one is that some of the axes are symmetrical, which is a lot
sentences.zh: 第一个理论的另一个问题是，有些手斧是对称的，如果你只是用它来砸坚果或

sentences.en: of extra effort that isn't really necessary if you're just using it to break up nuts or
sentences.zh: 切肉，

sentences.en: cut meat.
sentences.zh: 这就需要付出很多不必要的额外努力。

sentences.en: And so to address some of those problems, we get into theory number two, and this is my
sentences.zh: 为了解决其中一些问题，我们进入了第二种理论，这也是我

sentences.en: personal favorite, the sexy hand axe theory.
sentences.zh: 个人最喜欢的，性感手斧理论。

sentences.en: The quote unquote sexy hand axe theory proposes that these tools didn't have a use per se.
sentences.zh: 所谓“性感手斧”理论提出，这些工具本身并没有什么实用价值。

sentences.en: They were created mostly as a way of showing off.
sentences.zh: 它们主要是作为一种炫耀的方式而被创造出来的。

sentences.en: Like the feathers of a peacock.
sentences.zh: 就像孔雀的羽毛一样。

sentences.en: The goal wasn't to create a functional tool for butchering, but a symbolic tool for mate
sentences.zh: 其目的不是为了创造一个用于屠宰的功能性工具，而是为了创造一个用于吸引配偶的象征性工具。

sentences.en: attraction.
sentences.zh: 吸引配偶。

sentences.en: And making these things is really, really hard.
sentences.zh: 而且制造这些东西真的非常非常难。

sentences.en: Why spend so much time doing it unless you're showing off, right?
sentences.zh: 为什么要花这么多时间去做这事，除非你在炫耀，对吧？

sentences.en: You're showing the opposite sex what you can do.
sentences.zh: 你在向异性展示你的能力。

sentences.en: But there are a lot of experts who are doubtful of this one, including anthropologist Terrence
sentences.zh: 但许多专家对此表示怀疑，其中包括人类学家特伦斯·

sentences.en: Deacon.
sentences.zh: 迪肯。

sentences.en: Not all of them are beautiful teardrop shapes.
sentences.zh: 并不是所有手斧都是美丽的泪滴形。

sentences.en: They weren't all that nice and neat and symmetrical.
sentences.zh: 它们并非都那么精美、整洁和对称。

sentences.en: There is one interesting exception, and I mean one.
sentences.zh: 有一个有趣的例外，我说的是仅有的一个。

sentences.en: One beautiful 350,000-year-old exception.
sentences.zh: 一个历经 35 万年之久的精美例外。

sentences.en: A hand axe was located at the bottom of a kind of well in southern Spain.
sentences.zh: 一把手斧在西班牙南部一个类似水井的底部被发现。

sentences.en: It looks as though bodies were tossed down here, and one of the things it found in this well,
sentences.zh: 看起来好像有尸体被扔进这里，在这口井里发现的东西之一，

sentences.en: so to speak, it's just a cave well, is a hand axe that was made of a kind of rose quartz
sentences.zh: 姑且这么说吧，它只是一个洞穴水井，是一把由某种看起来像粉红石英制成的、

sentences.en: looking stuff, really pretty, and it doesn't look like it was ever used.
sentences.zh: 非常漂亮的手斧，而且看起来似乎从未被使用过。

sentences.en: Not a sexy hand axe, but this may be the first indications that they're beginning to sort of
sentences.zh: 这不是一把性感手斧，但这可能是最早的迹象，表明他们开始为某人的死

sentences.en: grieve over the death of someone or that there is some kind of ritual issue here in which a
sentences.zh: 感到悲伤，或者这里存在某种仪式问题，

sentences.en: beautiful hand axe is somehow playing a role.
sentences.zh: 在这其中一把漂亮的手斧在某种程度上发挥了作用。

sentences.en: Okay, okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧。

sentences.en: So Will's third favorite theory is still a really fun one.
sentences.zh: 所以威尔第三喜欢的理论依然是一个非常有趣的理论。

sentences.en: Number three is pretty fun.
sentences.zh: 第三个理论相当有趣。

sentences.en: Number three, and in a close follow-on to my favorite to sexy hand axe is the killer frisbee theory.
sentences.zh: 第三个理论，紧随我最喜欢的性感手斧之后，就是致命飞盘理论。

sentences.en: And so in the killer frisbee theory, right, hand axes were made to be projectiles.
sentences.zh: 所以在致命飞盘理论中，手斧被制作成抛射物。

sentences.en: So thrown in the fashion of the discus in the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 因此可以像奥运会中的铁饼一样被投掷出去。

sentences.en: A lot of hand axes are found near riverbanks.
sentences.zh: 许多手斧都是在河岸附近被发现的。

sentences.en: And so the hypothesis goes that hunters would wait for herds of animals to come, and then
sentences.zh: 于是有一种假设认为，猎人们会等待大群的动物到来，然后

sentences.en: they would bombard them with hand axes.
sentences.zh: 他们会用手斧对它们进行攻击。

sentences.en: This might not be enough to make a kill, but the stones would maim a few and give the hunters
sentences.zh: 这或许不足以致命，但石头会使一些动物受伤，并给猎人们

sentences.en: an opportunity to charge.
sentences.zh: 提供发起冲锋的机会。

sentences.en: This hypothesis, right, explains why it looks the way it does, right?
sentences.zh: 这种假设，对吧，解释了它为什么会呈现出现在的样子，对吗？

sentences.en: Why the hand axe is sharp all the way around, why it's so symmetrical, why it's so aerodynamic.
sentences.zh: 为什么手斧四周都很锋利，为什么它如此对称，为什么它如此符合空气动力学。

sentences.en: Well, again, not all of them are sharp all the way around and perfectly symmetrical.
sentences.zh: 好吧，话说回来，并不是所有手斧四周都那么锋利且完全对称。

sentences.en: Was it used like a frisbee, or was it used like a weapon?
sentences.zh: 它是像飞盘一样被使用，还是像武器一样被使用？

sentences.en: I really have my doubts about that.
sentences.zh: 我对这一点真的深表怀疑。

sentences.en: I like the Swiss Army knife view, in part because it looks like it's a one-tool-fits-all.
sentences.zh: 我挺喜欢瑞士军刀这种看法的，部分原因是因为它看起来像是一款万能工具。

sentences.en: It was clearly something that we see again and again and again and again, all over the world.
sentences.zh: 很显然，我们在世界各地一次又一次、不断地看到它的身影。

sentences.en: That means it was very effective, and if you don't find a lot of diversity of tools, it
sentences.zh: 这意味着它非常高效，如果你发现工具的种类并不丰富，那它

sentences.en: was almost certainly used for more than one thing.
sentences.zh: 几乎可以肯定是用于不止一种用途。

sentences.en: But whatever the hand axe was used for, it must have done a really good job, because this
sentences.zh: 但不管手斧是用来做什么的，它一定发挥得非常出色，因为这个

sentences.en: basic design was used for a mind-blowingly long time.
sentences.zh: 基本设计被使用了长得令人发指的时间。

sentences.en: Hominid adults were literally teaching hominid children how to make hand axes for more than
sentences.zh: 古人类成年人字面意义上是在教导古人类儿童如何制作手斧，持续了

sentences.en: a million years, passing the knowledge down from generation to generation.
sentences.zh: 一百万年以上，将这种知识一代又一代地传承下去。

sentences.en: And so you compare that to any modern product life cycle, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你把它跟任何现代产品生命周期相比，对吧？

sentences.en: It's just crazy long.
sentences.zh: 简直长得疯狂。

sentences.en: So long that our human minds can barely wrap our heads around it.
sentences.zh: 长到我们人类的大脑几乎无法理解的地步。

sentences.en: We have no conception of what that time frame is.
sentences.zh: 我们对那个时间跨度根本没有任何概念。

sentences.en: You know, our understanding of history is only, what, maybe 5,000, 10,000 years.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们对历史的理解只有，什么，也许五千年、一万年。

sentences.en: That's our biggest understanding of history.
sentences.zh: 那是我们对历史最大的理解了。

sentences.en: We're talking about something that stayed the same, a culture that was constant for
sentences.zh: 而我们现在讨论的是一个保持不变的事物，一个持续了

sentences.en: a million years.
sentences.zh: 一百万年的文化。

sentences.en: That's pretty remarkable.
sentences.zh: 这相当了不起。

sentences.en: And no matter what the Acheulean hand axe was actually used for, just the mere existence
sentences.zh: 而且无论阿舍利手斧实际上是用来做什么的，仅仅是这样一个古老的设计物体的存在

sentences.en: of a designed object that is so old has huge implications.
sentences.zh: 就有着巨大的意义。

sentences.en: I often have students or colleagues think that design's a new field, like a 20th century
sentences.zh: 我经常遇到学生或同事认为设计是一个新兴领域，比如说是20世纪的

sentences.en: invention, when in fact, it's the most ancient of all academic disciplines.
sentences.zh: 发明，然而事实上，它是所有学科中最古老的。

sentences.en: Before there was mathematics or engineering or science or art or music or poetry, before
sentences.zh: 在有数学、工程学、科学、艺术、音乐或诗歌之前，在

sentences.en: there was philosophy, literature, religion, or even language, there was design.
sentences.zh: 有哲学、文学、宗教甚至语言之前，就已经有了设计。
